name: Loofah
grown_as: A tender annual climber grown in a greenhouse or polytunnel in the UK, for its fibrous fruit (the bath sponge) or eaten young. Also listed as Luffa cylindrica.
habit: A vigorous climbing vine 3 to 5 m or more, stems five-angled and nearly hairless, climbing by branched tendrils (split into 2 to 6 coiling arms). Trained up wires or the roof of a greenhouse so the long fruit hang down.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, one at each joint, with a branched tendril beside it
leaf.outline: Rounded in outline, 15 to 25 cm across, cut into 5 to 7 triangular, pointed lobes, the cuts about a third of the way in
leaf.veins: Palmate, one main vein into each lobe, prominent beneath
leaf.surface: Rough above with short stiff hairs, paler beneath

flower.form: A large flat open flower, like a yellow saucer
flower.petals: Five, joined only at the very base so they look free, broad and rounded, spreading flat, finely veined
flower.centre: Male: three to five orange-yellow stamens in a small cluster. Female: a thick three-lobed stigma.
flower.behind: Five small pointed green sepals. Females sit on a long, slim, smooth ovary, the young loofah.
flower.carried: Males in long-stalked clusters (racemes) of 4 to 20 at the leaf joints, opening a few at a time; females singly on their own stalk at the same joint

fruit: A long, smooth, cylindrical fruit 30 to 60 cm by 5 to 8 cm, hanging from the vine, green with faint darker lengthways lines, a little thicker toward the far end. As it ripens it turns yellow then brown, the skin goes papery and peels off a dense network of pale fibres inside. Seeds flat, oval, black, about 12 mm, with a thin narrow wing-like rim; they rattle in the dried fruit.
seedling: Two smooth, oblong seed leaves; the first true leaf rough and lobed.
winter: Nothing: killed by cold. The dried fruit are peeled to make sponges.

leaf: a rounded leaf cut into 5 to 7 pointed triangular lobes
bloom: five broad rounded yellow petals spread flat like a saucer
a small cluster of stamens in the centre
seed: a thin rim round the edge
seedling: a small rough lobed true leaf
young: a climbing vine with leaves cut into 5 to 7 pointed lobes
branched tendrils with several coiling arms
flower: yellow saucer flowers in long-stalked clusters at the joints
crop: long smooth green cylindrical fruit hanging down from the vine
faint lengthways lines on the fruit

look_alikes: Angled loofah (Luffa acutangula) has fruit with ten sharp lengthways ridges. Cucumber has smaller flowers with joined petals and unbranched tendrils. Courgette leaves are prickly and its flowers are trumpets, not flat.
